q-222079.name: Question 1
q-222079.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=-2{x}^{2}+10x-3$ is $x=${{field-1}}.
q-222079.worked_solution:
The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

We substitute $a=-2$ and $b=10$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{10}{2(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{10}{(-4)} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{5}{2}.$

q-222074.name: Question 2
q-222074.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y={x}^{2}-8x-7$ is $x=${{field-1}}.
q-222074.worked_solution:
The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

We substitute $a=1$ and $b=-8$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{(-8)}{2(1)} \\  & =-\frac{(-8)}{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=4.$

q-13389.name: Question 3
q-13389.problem: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=3{x}^{2}-18x-3.$
q-13389.worked_solution:
The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry. 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=3$ and $b=-18$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{(-18)}{2(3)} \\  & =-\frac{(-18)}{6} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=3.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=3$ into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3{x}^{2}-18x-3 \\  & =3(3)^{2}-18(3)-3 \\  & =27-54-3 \\  & =-30\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is at $(3,-30).$

The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola y=ax2+bx+c is given by

x=−b2a.

q-106547.name: Question 4
q-106547.problem: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=-2{x}^{2}+4x-9.$
q-106547.worked_solution:
The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry. 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=-2$ and $b=4$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{4}{2(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{4}{(-4)} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=1.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=1$ into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2{x}^{2}+4x-9 \\  & =-2(1)^{2}+4(1)-9 \\  & =-2+4-9 \\  & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is at $(1,-7).$

The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola y=ax2+bx+c is given by

x=−b2a.

Substituting a=−2 and b=4 into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get x=−42(−2)=−4(−4)=1.

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is x=1. This also represents the x-coordinate of the vertex. To find the y-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute x=1 into the original equation: y=−2x2+4x−9=−2(1)2+4(1)−9=−2+4−9=−7

q-106548.name: Question 5
q-106548.problem: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=-4{x}^{2}-24x-10.$
q-106548.worked_solution:
The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry. 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=-4$ and $b=-24$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{(-24)}{2(-4)} \\  & =-\frac{(-24)}{(-8)} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=-3.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=-3$ into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4{x}^{2}-24x-10 \\  & =-4(-3)^{2}-24(-3)-10 \\  & =-36+72-10 \\  & =26\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is at $(-3,26).$

Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola y=−4x2−24x−10.

a
(−6,−10)
b
(3,−118)
c
(−3,−118)
d
(3,26)
e
(−3,26)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola y=ax2+bx+c is given by

x=−b2a.

Substituting a=−4 and b=−24 into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get x=−(−24)2(−4)=−(−24)(−8)=−3.

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is x=−3. This also represents the x-coordinate of the vertex. To find the y-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute x=−3 into the original equation: y=−4x2−24x−10=−4(−3)2−24(−3)−10=−36+72−10=26

Therefore, the vertex is at (−3,26).

q-222087.problem:
What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=-{x}^{2}-4x-3?$

The coordinates of the vertex are
$($
{{field-1}}

{{field-2}}

q-222087.worked_solution:
The parabola's vertex lies on the symmetry axis, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry. 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=-1$ and $b=-4$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{(-4)}{2(-1)} \\  & =-\frac{(-4)}{(-2)} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=-2.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=-2$ into the original equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-{x}^{2}-4x-3 \\  & =-(-2)^{2}-4(-2)-3 \\  & =-4+8-3 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is at $(-2,1).$

q-106551.name: Question 7
q-106551.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224554/assets/830944c0cff8aa0b2f1c58c9cd2ab7ae0f2560a9aa0e244796c0814ec99fd0c3.png)

Find the value of $k$ for the parabola $y=k{x}^{2}-4x-3,$ shown above.
q-106551.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since the graph tells us that the axis of symmetry is $x=2,$ we will set our result equal to $2.$ 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=k$ and $b=-4$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{(-4)}{2(k)} \\  & =\frac{4}{2k} \\  & =\frac{2}{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=2,$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{k} & =2 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-222095.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since the graph tells us that the axis of symmetry is $x=-2,$ we will set our result equal to $-2.$ 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=5$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{k}{2(5)} \\  & =-\frac{k}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-2,$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k}{10} & =-2 \\ -k & =-20 \\ k & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
